prompt: Our partners send us air quality data using the attached XSD (version 2.1). We're building a REST API and want a canonical data model behind it, so we can generate both the XSD-compatible structure and a JSON Schema for the API from one place. Please reverse-engineer the XSD into a data model, flag anything that's ambiguous or questionable in the XSD, and generate the JSON Schema. Each station produces about 24 hourly values per pollutant per day, ~400 stations, 6 pollutants. Just go ahead with your best judgement — I'll review afterwards.
assertions: A canonical model file exists separate from the generated JSON Schema
Position is modelled as a value type without its own identity (a datatype, or explicitly marked as an embedded value without a key)
Pollutant is modelled as an extensible or externally governed code list, not a closed enum or an undocumented plain string
The station kind is modelled as a closed enumeration with traffic, industrial and background
The meaning of the integer validity and verification codes is flagged as ambiguous
The missing coordinate reference system for lat/lon is flagged
Identifier issues are flagged (xs:ID values only unique within one document, and/or overlap of id and stationCode)
The observation volume (roughly 21 million per year: 400 x 6 x 24 x 365) is recorded in the canonical model, not only in prose
The high observation volume leads to an API design note (e.g. observations as a separate, paginated resource rather than nested in station documents)
The generated JSON Schema is a valid JSON Schema and allows null for the observation value
The JSON Schema keeps the observation value required but nullable, matching the XSD where the element is mandatory but nillable

An XSD generated from the canonical model accepts the same documents as the original 2.1 XSD: a sample delivery valid against observations.xsd also validates against the generated XSD (checked with lxml)

The pollutant code list is linked to a named standard vocabulary (e.g. the EEA/Eionet air quality pollutant vocabulary) with its register URI and a snapshot date or version, or reusing such a vocabulary is recommended to the user with the reason
